title: Segmentation (no target)
request: Let DCLab group customers that behave alike when there is no outcome to predict, and say honestly what such groups are worth.
spec: A segmentation kind: scaling and encoding choices recorded; k-means, Gaussian mixtures and HDBSCAN; the number of segments chosen by stability (bootstrap agreement) and silhouette, not by one run; each segment described in the data's own columns; an honest statement that no ground truth exists, and an optional check against a business outcome if one is named. Done when the replica (customers with three planted behaviours and noise) is recovered with stability intervals, and a too-high number of segments is rejected for instability.
plan: Record every preprocessing choice: scale, logs, one-hot weights, what is left out and why.
For each k and method, refit on bootstrap resamples and measure agreement with the full fit; keep a k only when the interval's lower end holds.
Require separation beyond what the same method finds on data with no groups, so a stable split of a flat table is not called segments.
Leave out columns no plausible grouping uses, then search again; profile each segment in the data's own columns.
Review, fix, and show each test fails on the fault it guards.

decisions.decision: Stability is necessary but not enough: a k must also be better separated than on data with no groups.
decisions.why: k-means splits a flat square into four quadrants stably every time; stable is not the same as grouped.

decisions.decision: The null is a Gaussian with the data's spread and a flat box over its ranges, not the columns shuffled.
decisions.why: Shuffling keeps each column's shape, so groups that live in one column's two humps looked like no groups at all.

decisions.decision: A column is left out only when no plausible grouping (stable, separated, near the best silhouette) uses it.
decisions.why: Judging columns by the first choice alone, usually k=2, dropped the column that tells the two smaller groups apart; judging by every grouping kept a noise column a fine split had sliced.

decisions.decision: The record states there is no ground truth, and a named outcome only describes the segments.
decisions.why: A segmentation that predicts an outcome well is a different problem; the outcome never forms the groups.

change: dclab_core/segment.py (prepare, stability, profiles, segment with two passes, _null_silhouette, _search, _report), dclab_core/replicas/customer_behaviours.py, dclab_rnd/kinds/segmentation.py, tests/test_core_segment.py, dclab_core/CHANGELOG.md, dclab_rnd/kinds/capability.json.

findings.defect: The shuffled-columns null called real groups in one column 'no groups'.
findings.scenario: 900 rows with x from two humps and two noise columns: k=2 perfectly stable, silhouette 0.351 against 0.353 shuffled, so nothing was chosen; a one-column table could never be segmented.
findings.cause: Shuffling keeps each column's marginal, so it tests dependence between columns, not groups.
findings.fix: The null is the best silhouette on a Gaussian with the data's spread and on a flat box over its ranges.

findings.defect: Column pruning dropped a column only a finer grouping used.
findings.scenario: Groups A (half), B and C: four columns split A from B and C, z splits B from C; the first pass chose k=2, z explained 0.1% under it and was dropped as unused, the final answer k=2 (agreement 0.73).
findings.cause: Columns were judged under the first chosen grouping only.
findings.fix: A column is dropped only when no plausible grouping (stable, separated, within 0.05 of the best silhouette) uses it.

findings.defect: The diagonal Gaussian mixture collapsed on one-hot columns.
findings.scenario: On replica seeds 1 to 3 the mixture at k=3 had stability lower ends 0.30 to 0.57 and the record blamed the data.
findings.cause: Binary dimensions drove a component's variance to zero.

findings.defect: The 'too many segments rejected' check could not catch a broken k-means stability gate.
findings.scenario: With k-means always marked stable, every test and the acceptance still passed: the mixture's instability supplied the rejected k.
findings.cause: The check accepted any method's rejection.
findings.fix: It requires a rejected k above the planted number for the chosen method.

findings.defect: The rejection reason stated the mean as below the bar.
findings.scenario: 'stability 0.879 (90% interval [0.738, 0.949]) below 0.75' was published though 0.879 is above 0.75.
findings.fix: It names the interval's lower end.

findings.defect: Prediction briefs were detected as segmentation.
findings.scenario: 'Predict which customers will churn next month, reported per customer segment' became segmentation, which the Solution then refuses.
findings.fix: Narrower words and no detection when the brief asks to predict, forecast or estimate.

findings.defect: A text or misspelt outcome failed silently.
findings.scenario: renewed as yes/no gave every segment a rate of None and 0 rows; outcome='renewal' dropped the section without a word.
findings.cause: to_numeric coerced the words to missing; a missing column was skipped.
findings.fix: Two levels in words are mapped and said; otherwise the record says why the outcome cannot describe the segments.

findings.defect: Tables under 15 rows crashed at the density view.
findings.scenario: An 8-row table raised from HDBSCAN after the whole search.
findings.fix: The density view is skipped below 30 rows.

findings.scenario: Median fills and a missing level were not recorded; an integer identifier was standardised and used.
findings.cause: Only text columns were tested for identifiers.
findings.fix: Fills and the missing level are recorded; an integer unique on every row is an identifier.

outcome: Built as a library and accepted on the replica (6 decisions, seeds 0 to 3); refused by the engine and partial in the matrix until the engine runs it.
lessons: Stable is not the same as grouped: compare with data that has no groups.
A null that keeps each column's shape tests dependence, not grouping.
Judge a column by every plausible grouping, not the first choice, and not the finest split.
A check another part of the system can satisfy is not a check of the part you meant.
risks: Segments reported in data with no groups.
A real signal column dropped as noise.
An outcome used to form the segments.
Segments presented as if they had a ground truth.
